io.lisp:77,92: fnn-store-fault and fnn-store-indeterminate are subclasses of fnn-store-error.
fix: In fnn-web-feed, catch only the semantic refusal that means 'connection unknown'. Let fnn-store-indeterminate and fnn-store-fault propagate, and give the ACL2 web session an :uncertain event. Wrap the accept loop the way fnn-mux-guarded does: send store-fault and serious-condition to fnn-owner-fault-service, and send indeterminate to fnn-owner-fence-service.
notes: 10-02 22:32 coded on lane/host-lifecycle 4e409a9d6 (handed to runner); see lanedumps/host-lifecycle.md for verification
reviewer: (1) fnn-web-feed (web-host.lisp:104-131) catches fnn-store-error, which is the parent of fnn-store-fault and fnn-store-indeterminate (io.lisp:74-92), and returns :gone. books/web-session.lisp:1895-1902 turns :gone into a redirect to /signin that drops the session, so an uncertain outcome is shown as session-lost. The owner itself does fence: fnn-owner-shared-action-locked (owner.lisp) stops the service before re-signalling. So the 'keeps running' part holds only for host-side faults outside fnn-owner-serialized, such as line 128 and the render path; those are swallowed and the node keeps running. (2) fnn-web-serve re-signals any non-socket, non-TLS error (lines 276-279). The thread's handler-case catches only socket-error (line 323). Host faults outside serialized calls (lines 155, 169, 195, 203, 225, 263) escape the thread, and so does the fnn-refuse 'owner service is stopping' from fnn-web-open during a stop race. None of these reach fnn-owner-fault-service. The image runs with --disable-debugger (build.lisp:622), so an unhandled error there leaves the 3/4 exit-code discipline. Most of the fault triggers need malformed ACL2 output. The uncertain-shown-as-gone and stop-race paths are reachable.
scenario: (1) fnn-web-feed catches fnn-store-error, and that class includes fnn-store-fault and fnn-store-indeterminate. Suppose a web POST's drain is uncertain, so the shared action stops the owner and re-signals indeterminate. The ACL2 session is told (:gone), which is the 'owner forgot CID' event. The browser therefore gets the session-lost page instead of an uncertain 'do not repost' answer, and the user reposts. A host-side fnn-fault in this function never reaches the owner at all: 'consumed no octets' and malformed render windows are converted to :gone and the node keeps running on a broken invariant. (2) In fnn-web-request, a host fault such as the event-budget exhaustion at line 240, a malformed head, frame or action, or the peer-address check is re-signalled by fnn-web-serve. The accept thread catches only socket-error (line 323). The error therefore leaves the thread without fnn-owner-fault-service: either the web thread dies and the listener keeps accepting into a backlog nobody serves, or SBCL's --disable-debugger exit path ends the process with code 1, skipping the fence and the 3/4 exit codes. The comment says 'an ACL2 fault is the owner's (it stopped)', but nothing on this path stops the owner.
title: Web face: host faults escape the thread without fencing, and a store fault or indeterminate outcome is reported to the session as :gone
